I'm 65 this year, and I've been farming these flat lands of Quzhou County on the North China Plain for over four decades. Back when I was young, I was one of the few in my village who finished high school, and that education taught me to read the agricultural bulletins and listen carefully to the extension technicians from China Agricultural University — they've been working in Quzhou since the 1970s, back when we were still fighting the salt-alkali soils. My children have long since moved to the city for work, so it's just me and my wife managing the land now. I hold 6 mu of good, flat land, and I know this soil like the back of my hand.

This year, like most years, I'll stick with the wheat-corn double cropping system. It's the only rotation that truly makes sense here — the soil is fertile, the market is stable, and I have access to the machinery I need. My winter wheat is already in the ground from last October; I planted an improved variety, Jimai 22, which handles our dry, cold winters reliably. Come early June, right after the wheat harvest, I'll plant Deng Hai 605 hybrid maize straight into the wheat stubble using no-tillage seeding. That saves me precious days during the busiest transition of the year and keeps every drop of soil moisture where it belongs.

I'm not one to waste inputs. With the groundwater table dropping every year in Hebei, I've learned to be careful with water. I'll irrigate the wheat three times — one winter irrigation to protect against the cold, one at jointing, and one at grain filling. For the corn, twice will be enough: once at the jointing stage and once at filling. I base my fertilizer on what the soil needs and what the extension agents recommend, not on habit. I'll put down about 25 kg of nitrogen per mu for the wheat and 20 kg for the corn, balanced with phosphorus and potassium. For pest control, I'll spray three times for the wheat and twice for the corn, tank-mixing herbicide, insecticide, or fungicide when the weather and the pests call for it. If the season cooperates, I expect about 1,050 kg per mu from the wheat and 1,100 kg per mu from the corn. This is my land, and I trust what I know.
